notes.text: David Jiříček has started playing on the power play: on the ice for 41% of the team’s power-play time in 10 games, up from 2% last season.

The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 20% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the lowest share in the league (a typical team: 39%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Jordan Kyrou is out (upper body injury) and missed their last game. He is one of their most valuable skaters.

Rasmus Sandin is out long term and has missed the last 17 games. He is a top-four defenseman. Timothy Liljegren has taken his spot beside Martin Fehérváry. That pair has had 53% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 121:13 together.
Justin Holl returned in their last game after missing 5 games. Their recent numbers were built mostly without him.
Jakob Chychrun has started killing penalties: on the ice for 25% of the team’s shorthanded time in 21 games, up from 8% last season.

stakes: The Capitals go in sixth in the Metropolitan with 20 points, 4 points behind the Flyers, fifth.

story.head: Tuch’s favorite opponent
paras: The Capitals won the teams’ first meeting this season, 5-2 in Washington on Oct 28. The Caps are on a five-game losing streak, while the Flyers have won three straight. This is a Metropolitan Division matchup, with the Flyers fifth (tied for 19th in the NHL) and the Capitals sixth (26th).

The Flyers’ record (.462) is about what their chances are worth. The Capitals have played better than their record (.476) says: their chances are worth about .574, and their goaltending has held them back.
In their five-game skid, the Capitals have been outscored 30-16, including 17-10 at 5-on-5.

The Flyers play slow, tight games (2nd lowest), take away shots from the point (3rd lowest) and pick their shots (4th lowest). Philadelphia has scored 2.58 goals a game, the fourth fewest in the league. As for the Capitals, they get their shots through to the net (4th), but give up a lot of dangerous shots (29th). They also get the league’s best looks (1st), so the Capitals have the edge over the Flyers on shot quality. Washington has allowed 3.95 goals a game, the third most in the league. The Capitals’ knack for getting shots through meets the Flyers’ shot blockers.

Matvei Michkov (11 G / 9 A / 20 P in 26 GP) leads the Flyers in scoring, and Christian Dvorak (5 G / 10 A / 15 P in 26 GP) is next in line. For the Capitals, Dylan Strome (4 G / 14 A / 18 P in 21 GP) leads the way in scoring. Alex Tuch (14 G / 3 A / 17 P in 21 GP) has a team-high 14 goals, tied for seventh in the NHL, with a point in eight straight games against Philadelphia.
Joseph Woll (5-6-2 / .892 SV% in 13 GS) is expected to start for Philadelphia, and Logan Thompson (7-6-0 / .879 SV% in 15 GS) for Washington.

items.text: The Capitals are newly without Jordan Kyrou, and have been without Rasmus Sandin for several games. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, no team is missing more right now.
Alex Ovechkin has one goal on chances worth about 5.6 goals, well below what his finishing usually turns chances into. If the chances keep coming, so should the goals.
Trevor Zegras is two goals from 100.
Ryan Leonard has a point in five straight games.
